report: Resident A had a comfortable night with adequate pain management. Family visited and expressed satisfaction with the care provided.
Resident B showed signs of increased fatigue and requested additional pain medication. Physician notified for further assessment.
Resident C demonstrated improved spirits after a visit from the hospice chaplain. Ongoing monitoring of pain and symptoms needed.
Resident D's family requested a meeting to discuss end-of-life care options. Social worker notified to facilitate the conversation.
Resident E experienced a peaceful passing surrounded by loved ones. Comfort measures were maintained until the final moments.

Resident A is currently receiving palliative care for end-stage cancer. During morning assessment, resident was found to be in moderate pain and requested pain medication. Resident's family was contacted and informed of resident's condition. Pain medication was administered as prescribed and resident's pain decreased significantly.

Resident B has been experiencing increasing shortness of breath over the past week. Oxygen saturation levels were monitored this morning and found to be slightly decreased. Resident is now on continuous oxygen therapy to help improve symptoms. Resident's family was updated on the change in care plan and is supportive of the decision.

Resident C has been showing signs of increased confusion and restlessness. A family meeting was held this morning to discuss resident's condition and the need for increased comfort measures. It was decided to start resident on a new medication to help manage these symptoms. Nursing staff will continue to monitor resident closely for any changes in behavior.

Resident D has been experiencing weight loss and decreased appetite. An assessment this morning revealed a further decline in nutritional intake. A consultation with the dietitian was requested to determine the best plan of action to increase resident's food intake. Family members were notified of the situation and will be involved in the decision-making process.

Resident E has been experiencing increased weakness and fatigue. A physical therapy session this morning revealed a decline in strength and mobility. Nursing staff will continue to collaborate with the therapy team to provide resident with the necessary support and assistive devices to help maintain independence as much as possible. Family members were consulted and are in agreement with the updated care plan.
